title: Proxy blocks hostile fetches and untrusted instructions
description:
Build the first controlled-fetch security slice for the Rust agent gateway. The proxy must fail closed for SSRF destinations including private, loopback, link-local, and cloud metadata addresses; revalidate every DNS resolution and redirect hop; enforce redirect, content-type, and response-size limits; wrap remote content as explicitly untrusted data; quarantine known prompt-injection patterns; block when classification is uncertain; and return bounded safe reason codes and correlation identifiers without echoing secrets or hostile payloads.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a fetch request targeting a private, loopback, link-local, or cloud metadata address, when the proxy resolves the destination before connecting, then it blocks with a safe reason code and correlation id without echoing the target payload.
2. Given a public resolution followed by DNS rebinding or TOCTOU to a private address, when the proxy connects, then it blocks at the socket boundary before sending data.
3. Given a 3xx response, when the redirect target is evaluated, then the full destination policy is reapplied on every hop.
4. Given a redirect chain exceeding the configured maximum, when the limit is reached, then the proxy blocks with an excessive-redirect reason.
5. Given a disallowed content type or oversized body, when response headers are inspected, then the body is not forwarded.
6. Given safe external content, when returned to an agent, then it is wrapped in an explicit untrusted-data envelope that cannot change gateway policy or tool permissions.
7. Given content matching the versioned prompt-injection policy, when classified, then it is quarantined or flagged and not delivered as trusted instructions.
8. Given uncertain classification below the policy threshold, when content is classified, then delivery fails closed.
9. Given any blocked request, when the response is generated, then it contains only a safe reason code and correlation id and does not echo secrets or the full hostile payload.
